title: Cash & Cash Equivalents
description: Understand what qualifies as cash and how cash equivalents are treated.
html:
What counts as cash?

Cash includes money that is readily available for use.

Common examples

  • Currency and coins
  • Demand deposits
  • Checking accounts
  • Undeposited customer checks

Cash equivalents

Cash equivalents are short-term, highly liquid investments that can be converted quickly into known amounts of cash and generally have insignificant risk of changes in value.

They generally have an original maturity of three months or less.

Example

A company purchases a Treasury bill when it has two months remaining until maturity.

Assuming the other requirements are met, it may qualify as a cash equivalent.

Restricted cash

Sometimes cash cannot be used freely because it has been set aside for a particular purpose.

This is called restricted cash.

Important distinction

Cash may physically exist but still require separate presentation or disclosure if its use is restricted.

Items that are not automatically cash

  • Postdated checks
  • Employee IOUs
  • Long-term investments
  • Receivables from customers

quiz.prompt: Which investment is most likely to qualify as a cash equivalent?

choices.text: A bond purchased with five years remaining until maturity
Common stock expected to be sold within three months
A one-year certificate of deposit purchased eleven months ago
A Treasury bill purchased when it has two months remaining until maturity

quiz.explanation: Cash equivalents are highly liquid short-term investments, generally with original maturities of three months or less.
